edges.target_label: From Pixels to States: World Models as Game Engines (2026)
edges.note: Where World Models learn an implicit latent recurrent state to predict observations, this paper argues for an explicit rule-following game state that persists over long horizons and supplies ground-truth states to train and measure against.

edges.target_label: From Pixels to States: World Models as Game Engines (2026)
edges.note: Where Navigation World Models condition prediction on actions for navigation, this paper reframes the target as a game engine's action-state-observation loop and releases a dataset with ground-truth states.

edges.target_label: From Pixels to States: World Models as Game Engines (2026)
edges.note: Offline RL is the reference for learning from logged interaction without live rollouts; this paper supplies over 90 hours of logged gameplay with frame-aligned actions and ground-truth states for state-aware world modeling.

edges.target_label: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong (2026)
edges.note: Where World Models treat the learned model as a source of control and robustness, BadWAM treats the coupling of imagination and action as an attack surface.

edges.target_label: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong (2026)
edges.note: Navigation World Models condition planning on predicted futures; BadWAM shows small perturbations can hijack the action while the predicted future still looks correct.

edges.source_label: From Pixels to States: World Models as Game Engines (2026)
edges.target_label: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong (2026)
edges.note: Where From Pixels to States argues explicit state improves control, BadWAM shows that if imagination and action are only loosely coupled the imagination can look right while the action is already wrong.

edges.target_label: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation (2026)
edges.note: Where Navigation World Models conditioned prediction on an action and left the model to infer what the action implies about the scene, DreamX-Phi hands the model the transformation explicitly so arm identity cannot be confused.

edges.target_label: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation (2026)
edges.note: Where DINO-WM froze a self-supervised encoder to define the latent space the model plans in, here the frozen V-JEPA teacher supervises one masked region and the model stays in pixel space, so the self-supervised asset acts as a regulariser rather than as the state representation.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT conditions a transformer diffusion backbone through adaptive normalisation and keeps attention purely positional, DreamX-Phi changes what attention sees by encoding rigid-motion structure into it.

edges.target_label: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation (2026)
edges.note: Ha and Schmidhuber framed a learned forward model of observations as a substitute for the environment; DreamX-Phi keeps that framing and makes the substitute faithful to the commanded action rather than only plausible.

edges.target_label: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?

edges.target_label: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
edges.note: Vafa showed a model can score well on next-step prediction while holding an incoherent internal world model; PAWBench moves the same argument from internal state to output distribution.

edges.target_label: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: Ha and Schmidhuber compressed observations into a learned latent state; this paper replaces that latent state with source code so the representation can be read and checked.

edges.target_label: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: Vafa showed a model can predict well while holding an incoherent world model; an executable program makes coherence enforceable by rendering and comparison rather than by probing.

edges.target_label: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: PyVision had an agent write throwaway analysis code to answer a visual question; here the agent writes code that is itself the persistent scene representation and is reused as training data.
